description: A multidisciplinary team passionate about space exploration, AI, and innovative problem-solving. We combine our technical skills and creativity to develop intelligent solutions that support safer and more efficient space missions.
summary:
StarryNight is an evidence-first fire-safety analysis platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Cairo 2026 challenge, *Flame in Freefall*. It transforms NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion experiments into actionable, traceable insights for spacecraft, the International Space Station (ISS), Moon and Mars habitats, and pressurized rovers.

The platform addresses a critical challenge: fire behaves differently in microgravity, while existing NASA experiments do not fully cover the oxygen concentrations, pressures, and partial-gravity conditions expected in future exploration habitats. StarryNight analyzes 24 NASA combustion investigations through an interactive web application featuring scenario evaluation, gravity bounds, habitat-specific investigation ranking, evidence comparisons, and an AI-powered analyst with clickable citations.

Its key innovation is combining deterministic, evidence-based verdicts with AI-generated explanations while preventing unsupported conclusions. When experimental evidence is insufficient, the platform explicitly communicates that limitation rather than guessing.

By making existing research accessible and exposing critical knowledge gaps, StarryNight supports safer spacecraft design, better-targeted experiments, and improved fire-safety decisions for future human space exploration.
details: StarryNight is a web app that turns NASA’s space fire experiments into clear fire-safety answers for spacecraft, the International Space Station, and future Moon and Mars bases. Future habitats are planned to use more oxygen at lower pressure, which makes materials easier to burn. NASA’s 263 solid-material space fire tests, however, were all run in ordinary cabin air at about zero gravity. A user picks a material and a place, or asks a question in plain words. StarryNight shows what NASA’s tests found, links every fact to the exact NASA record, and says clearly when no test covers the case instead of guessing. It also ranks NASA’s 24 combustion investigations for each type of habitat, maps conditions that have never been tested, and provides clean datasets for engineers and researchers. It is built only on NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics data, is live today, and is checked by 139 automated tests.
